title: Regression Sheriff: adaptive halt & quarantine policy for staged rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an adaptive ‘Regression Sheriff’ controller that monitors fine-grained eval signals during Canary and A/B rollouts and takes graduated actions: throttle traffic, quarantine cohorts, or trigger automated rollback. Unlike existing static threshold gates, this controller uses short-window drift scoring, confidence-weighted metric aggregation, and a quarantine policy to isolate suspicious cohorts while preserving overall availability. Goals: (1) reduce noisy false-positive rollbacks by 50% vs current naive gates, (2) limit customer-facing error surface by quarantining at most 5% of traffic for transient anomalies, and (3) provide explainable rollback rationale to SRE/PM/Customer Success teams.
updates: 2026-02-10: Spec draft completed and reviewed by PM/Design. Key requirement: allow staged actions (throttle/quarantine/rollback) and human-in-the-loop escalation for high-impact customers.

2026-02-17: Prototype controller built in k8s as a control-plane deployment that subscribes to per-cohort eval streams. Initial offline sims run with historical canopy datasets (12M inference events) to tune short-window (30s/5m) detectors.

2026-02-20: Sim results: short-window drift detector catches injected regressions (5-10% quality drop) within median 47s; naive fixed-threshold gate median detection 210s. False positive rate in sim for our policy ~2.7% vs 6.2% baseline.

2026-02-25: Design review feedback from Security: quarantine action must preserve PII isolation and respect Private deployment constraints; added KMS key usage in logs and redact sample payloads in alerts.

2026-03-01: Integration spike with Console: added a new ‘sheriff actions’ UI panel to show quarantined cohorts, action history, and rollback provenance. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298

2026-03-06: Canary in staging: enabled on canary cohort for runtime-1.21 with conservative settings (quarantine_threshold=3sigma, max_quarantine_pct=3%). Observed one transient metric blip in responses/sec correlated with upstream infra GC; sheriff quarantined 1.2% traffic and automatically healed after 90s. No customer impact.

2026-03-12: Load testing and chaos run: validated that quarantine and gradual rollback keep latency SLO within 8% of baseline while maintaining 99.9% availability for primary cohort. Next: harden alert text and add automated Jira/Playbook links for ops runbooks.
comments: PM (Lina Gomez): We need strong explainability for any automated rollback; include a machine-readable rationale blob in the audit event so support can triage quickly.
Design (Rajiv Kapoor): Console mocks look good; recommend adding a timeline scrubber to inspect metric windows that led to quarantine decisions.
SRE (Emily Chen): Verify that quarantine does not cause cache stampedes for downstream services; add circuit breaker on per-model route.
Lead Eng (Marcus Nguyen): Opted for controller-level policy rather than embedding in runtime to keep rollout logic orthogonal to model execution. Will revisit if latency becomes a concern.
Security (Omar Farouk): Confirmed redaction rules; any sample included in the alert must be truncated and hashed; added requirement in QA checklist.
